func (a *app) showGrammar() bool {
	a.section("GRAMÁTICA")
	a.print(a.grammar.String())
	a.print(fmt.Sprintf("\nSímbolo inicial: %s\n", a.grammar.Start))
	a.print(fmt.Sprintf("Não terminais:   %s\n", strings.Join(a.grammar.NonTerminals, " ")))
	a.print(fmt.Sprintf("Terminais:       %s (fim da entrada: %s)\n\n", strings.Join(a.grammar.Terminals, " "), ll1.EndMarker))
	a.print("Produções numeradas (os números aparecem na tabela de parsing):\n")
	a.print(a.productionList())
	return true
}

BuildTable
nodes.doc: BuildTable fills the table from FIRST and FOLLOW: production A -> α goes in M[A, a] for every terminal a in FIRST(α), and, when ε is in FIRST(α), in M[A, b] for every b in FOLLOW(A). A cell claimed twice is a conflict; the first production keeps the cell.

nodes.label: Generate
nodes.doc: Generate builds a random valid sentence by a leftmost derivation from the start symbol. Below maxDepth every production is equally likely; from maxDepth on, only the productions that finish the derivation fastest are chosen. Tokens are joined by spaces: "x + 3 * ( y )".
nodes.signature: func Generate(g *Grammar, rng *rand.Rand, maxDepth int) string

nodes.label: GenerateInvalid
nodes.doc: GenerateInvalid mutates a valid sentence (drops a token, duplicates an operator, adds an unbalanced parenthesis or inserts an illegal character) and retries until the parser rejects the result.

nodes.label: Grammar.First
nodes.doc: First computes FIRST of every non-terminal with the fixed-point algorithm. Each set is ordered like Terminals, with ε last when present.

nodes.label: Grammar.FirstOfSequence
nodes.doc: FirstOfSequence returns FIRST of a sequence of symbols, ordered like Terminals with ε last. An empty sequence (or just ε) gives {ε}.

nodes.label: Grammar.Follow
nodes.doc: Follow computes FOLLOW of every non-terminal with the fixed-point algorithm. Each set is ordered like Terminals, with $ last when present.

nodes.label: unexpected
cmd/analisador
nodes.doc: Command analisador is the terminal front end of the LL(1) predictive table-driven parser: it shows the grammar, the FIRST and FOLLOW sets and the parsing table, and traces the recognition of typed or generated sentences.

nodes.label: cmd/codegraph
nodes.doc: Command codegraph reads the Go source of this module and writes a JSON graph (packages, files, types, functions, methods and the edges between them) that the /graph page draws.

nodes.label: cmd/wasm
nodes.doc: Command wasm exposes the ll1 package to the browser as globalThis.ll1. Every function returns a JSON string, except generate and generateInvalid, which return the sentence itself.

nodes.label: ll1
nodes.doc: Package ll1 implements a table-driven (non-recursive) predictive LL(1) parser for a fixed arithmetic expression grammar: FIRST and FOLLOW sets, the parsing table, a lexer, the stack parser and a sentence generator.
